title: Thank you @Lincoln Center for bringing back Shuffle Along so it can f...
transcript: I just had one of the most incredible nights at the theatre, attending the shuffle Along reunion concert, starring most of the original cast, including Audra McDonald, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Billy Porter and Norm Lewis stepping in for the role originally played by Josh Henry. And that's not even to mention the several supporting performers who at the time were virtually unknown, but now are stars in their own right. People like Amber Iman, Adrienne Warren, Brandon Victor Dixon. When I say it was a stacked cast, it was a stacked cast. And this was one of those shows that never quite got the attention it deserved. It was, of course, the same season as Hamilton, and so it got largely overshadowed. And since the show was never recorded, it never got a cast album, a lot of people really never got a chance to discover it. It tells the true story of the creation of the musical Shuffle Along, a show written by four black men with an all black cast, and is the show that is credited with bringing jazz to Broadway for the first time. And yet, despite being this massive hit and this landmark achievement of black theatre, it was largely forgotten to history until this musical came along to tell its story. And now, 10 years later, here it is, being performed again for two nights only. And while this is being billed as a concert, this very much felt like a remount. It Was fully staged by director George C. Wolfe, and Savion Glover came back to recreate all of his iconic choreography. And let me tell you, seeing Audra do that iconic leg kick in person was worth the price of admission alone, which, by the way, was pay what you can for every single seat in the house. Which is a stark contrast to a lot of the reunion concerts we usually get, which, yes, are for charity, but do often fetch a hefty ticket price, sometimes in the thousands and tens of thousands of dollars a ticket. This show is so important for so many reasons, and I am so glad that it was made accessible to everyone, regardless of economic status. Not only that, but the concert is also being recorded for PBS Great Performances, making it the first time that this show has ever been recorded. So even people that weren't able to be in the room because those tickets went quickly will still be able to watch it for free on PBS, And experience this incredible story told by this legendary cast. And I'm just so excited that the show is finally going to be discovered by so many people.
